name: Ram Damage Model
description: Turns closing speed and mass into collision damage, with crumple thresholds that mark when a hit was structural. It exists because in a vehicular combat game the bumper is the most-used weapon, and if ramming is just physics knockback there is no game. This component owns the speed-times-mass formula and the self-damage fraction that makes a reckless T-bone cost the attacker too. It does not subtract health itself: computed damage is handed to combat.damage_resolver, so armor, resistances, and status effects keep one home, and a shielded target mitigates a ram the same way it mitigates a shell. Crumple is reported as an event for combat.vehicle_damage_states and presentation to consume; this model does not decide what crumpling means for handling or visuals.

inputs.name: massTons
inputs.description: Vehicle mass used in the damage formula. Heavy builds hit harder and take less relative self-damage, which is the entire reason to drive a truck.

inputs.name: damagePerSpeedMass
inputs.description: Conversion from closing speed times mass to base damage. Tune against expected top speeds so a full-speed head-on is decisive but not instantly lethal.

inputs.name: selfDamageFraction
inputs.description: Share of dealt damage the rammer takes back. At 0 ramming is free and every race becomes a demo derby; at 1 it is a last resort.

inputs.name: crumpleSpeedThreshold
inputs.description: Closing speed above which the collision counts as structural and combat.vehicleCrumpled fires. Below it the hit is a bump — damage only, no state change.

outputs.name: lastRamSpeed
outputs.description: Closing speed of the most recent ram, exposed for kill-feed flavor and drift-scoring drop logic.
